title: card-profile
description: One reference-model card, defined. Every claim-bearing field is a `claim` object that either cites records and carries a verbatim quote from their SOURCE text, or is marked proposed. There is no third option: a field with no evidence is either absent or proposed. Nothing here may be asserted.

status.description: carried from the reference model, not re-decided here

definition.description: what this element is, in one or two sentences

standards.description: standards governing this element. An empty array is a real answer and must be explained in gaps.

id.description: directory name under standards/, e.g. oci-runtime-spec

role.description: what part of this card the standard actually governs

covers.description: what it does NOT cover, where that matters

tools.description: real implementations that fill this slot today

in_use_here.description: true only if this repo actually uses it

landscape.description: how the options differ and what the real tradeoff is

usage.description: how a caller uses this element - the shape of the call, not a tutorial

gaps.description: what is missing, unsettled or uncited. An empty list is itself a claim and is usually wrong.

research_query.description: the search that would close it

claim.description: The unit of trust. origin=sourced carries `evidence`: one {id, quote} pair per cited record, where each quote appears verbatim in that record's SOURCE text (its snippet or read field) - never in the record's own claim field, which is this repo's prose about a source. A citation is an id AND a quote together: an id with no quote is decoration, since nothing ties the record to the claim, and it cannot be expressed in this shape. origin=proposed carries no evidence and its text must say so.

evidence.description: required when origin is sourced; every cited record brings its own quote

quote.description: verbatim substring of THIS record's snippet or read
